rules: The ball must be kicked with the foot or leg.
Fielders can get a runner out by tagging them with the ball or hitting them with the ball below the shoulders.
Force outs occur when a runner must advance to the next base and the fielder touches the base with the ball.
You may not advance on a caught ball ever (No tag ups)
No strike outs and your team provides your own pitcher; pitcher needs to kick too
No leading off or stealing bases; runners must stay on the base until the ball is kicked.
Kick in order (nobody kicks a second time until everyone has kicked once)
Anything close goes to runner
Ball must go into main gym before touching anything or anyone or it is a foul ball

key_terms.definition: An out made when a runner is forced to move to the next base and the fielder touches that base while holding the ball.
The set sequence in which players on the offensive team must take their turn to kick.
When a fly ball is caught, a runner must touch their original base after the catch before trying to advance.

global_connections.description: While popular in American schools, kickball has grown into massive adult social leagues across the United States and is frequently played as a community-building sport.

activities.name: Game play
rules: Played indoors with large 8'x4' mats for bases and a Scoring Line defined by two cones at home.
A Charge Line is designated just past 1st and 3rd base.
There is only ONE out per inning. The moment an out is recorded, the teams switch sides.
Mercy Rule: An inning automatically ends when the offense scores 15 runs. A home run clearing the bases is the only way to exceed this.
The pitcher must roll the ball from the outfield, and it must pass exactly between the two scoring line cones.
Pitching Penalty: If the pitch misses the cones, all active runners advance one base (or the kicker takes 2nd if bases are empty).
The kicked ball must cross the Charge Line past 1st and 3rd base, otherwise it is a foul ball.
Pace of Play: The pitcher can roll the instant the defense resets. If the next kicker isn't ready at the cones, they are OUT.
Multiple runners are allowed on a single base at the same time.
Baserunners can start running the exact moment the ball is kicked.
There are absolutely no force outs on the field.
The entire defense must start in the outfield and cannot cross the Charge Line until the kicked ball crosses it first.
The single out is achieved by catching a fly ball, tagging a runner, throwing and hitting a runner (pegging), or the next kicker penalty.
